i18n.currencyFormatting: `private fun formatRupees(paise: Long): String = "₹%,.0f".format(paise / 100.0)` — EarningsScreen.kt:384. Uses the ₹ glyph (good) but: (a) `%,.0f` inherits the JVM default Locale, so lakh/crore grouping is not pinned — grouping style silently varies with device locale rather than being explicitly Indian; (b) `.0f` ROUNDS paise rather than truncating or showing them, so ₹1,234.56 renders as ₹1,235 — a technician reconciling cash will see a number that does not match the ledger; (c) the same helper in the LIVE Pay tab is `"Rs %,.0f"` (technician-app/app/src/main/kotlin/com/homeservices/technician/ui/home/TechnicianHomeScreen.kt:1350) — two different currency renderings ship in one app.

The cash-commission / receivable model (E21-S01, api/src/cosmos/commission-receivable-repository.ts, api/src/functions/technicians/commission-due.ts) is NOT surfaced anywhere in technician-app — a grep for receivable|commission|cashCollected over technician-app/app/src/main/kotlin returns zero hits. observations.evidence: technician-app/app/src/main/kotlin/com/homeservices/technician/domain/earnings/model/EarningsSummary.kt:26-33 (model has only today/week/month/lifetime/lastSevenDays/pendingHeldPaise — no commission or receivable field)

observations.claim: Two different rupee renderings ship in the same app: '₹%,.0f' here vs 'Rs %,.0f' ASCII in the live Pay tab.
`pendingHeldPaise` — the only money field that represents un-paid-out balance — exists on the model but is never rendered on this screen.

No period-over-period comparison anywhere — four absolute totals with no delta, no 'vs last week', no trend arrow. The only comparative signal is a 7-bar Canvas with no y-axis, no values, and no tooltip.
Money is rounded to whole rupees, so displayed earnings can disagree with the ledger by up to 50 paise per figure.
GoalProgressCard divides by `month.goalPaise` with no zero guard — if the API returns goalPaise=0 the Float division yields NaN/Infinity before coerceIn.

Four unmapped M3 typography slots are used (titleMedium x2, headlineSmall, labelMedium), each of which falls back to Roboto instead of Geist Sans / Noto Devanagari — the screen mixes typefaces including on its own page heading.
The two bottom actions are both full-width OutlinedButtons stacked identically — no primary action, no visual hierarchy, and they read as a pair of dead gray bars closing the screen.
The Canvas sparkline has zero accessibility semantics and zero interaction — no per-bar value, no press feedback, no contentDescription.

TopAppBar applies the gradient via Modifier.background on the TopAppBar itself while forcing transparent container colors — the gradient will not extend under the status bar inset the way a Surface-based header would.
Weekday label falls back to a literal '?' on parse failure, which would render as an untranslated glyph in the chart axis.

observations.claim: DIVERGENCE FROM CUSTOMER APP — the two apps implement the same feature with completely different chrome. Customer: no Scaffold, a bare Surface + statusBarsPadding + 24.dp padding, an HsTrustBadge 'Settings', an HsScreenTitle at headlineSmall, and an inline HsPrimaryButton. Technician: a Scaffold with a real TopAppBar (titleMedium), a back arrow, an elevated bottomBar, a plain M3 Button (not HsPrimaryButton), a subtitle line, and 18/20.dp gutters. Same product, two unrelated designs.
The technician Save control is a raw MaterialTheme Button, bypassing the design system's HsPrimaryButton which the customer app uses for the identical action.
No error handling of any kind — a failed locale persist is indistinguishable from success.

observations.claim: The content Column is fillMaxSize + Arrangement.Center with NO verticalScroll, so on a small screen or in Hindi (or with large font scale) the 'Done' button — the only way to complete sign-out via the UI — can be pushed off-screen.
An unparseable timestamp is echoed raw into user-facing copy, exposing an ISO-8601 string inside a sentence.
The external-browser Intent is launched with no ActivityNotFoundException guard.

The 'Done' button uses the raw M3 Button with default width (not fillMaxWidth, not HsPrimaryButton), so the terminal CTA is a small pill floating under full-width content — a hierarchy failure at the end of a destructive flow.
Two different date-formatting strategies coexist in the app: localized FormatStyle.LONG here vs a hardcoded 'dd MMM yyyy' pattern on MyRatings.
Pressing 'Done' fires an async clearSession with no busy/disabled state, so double-taps are possible.
The revocation instructions embed a support email address in a non-selectable, non-tappable Text — the user cannot copy or mailto it.
The design system is not used at all on this screen — no com.homeservices.designsystem import appears in lines 3-36.
